prompt: How do I sign up for an account on practiceyourspeech.com?
chosen: You can register on practiceyourspeech.com using either native credentials (email and password, which requires clicking a verification link sent via Amazon SES) or directly using Google OAuth.
rejected: Just click sign up and fill it out. Or use Google. It doesn't really matter.

prompt: I didn't get my email verification link. What do I do?
chosen: Please check your spam or junk folder, as the email is sent via Amazon SES. Verify that your email was typed correctly on your profile page. If it still doesn't arrive, contact support and an administrator will manually toggle your verification status in the database.
rejected: If you didn't get the email, there's a problem with your mail provider. We can't do anything about it. Try registering again with a different email.

prompt: How can I change my password?
chosen: If you signed up using native credentials, you can change your password directly in your Profile tab under 'Change Password'. Google OAuth users do not store a password on our system and cannot use this form.
rejected: Just click change password in settings. If it's not working, you probably signed up with Google so you can't.

prompt: Can I use password reset if I registered with Google?
chosen: No, because Google OAuth accounts do not store passwords on our platform. You must authenticate using the 'Continue with Google' button.
rejected: No, Google users don't have passwords. You are out of luck if you want a password.

prompt: What happens if I forget my password?
chosen: You can request a password reset on the sign-in page. The system generates a verification token and emails a secure reset link via Amazon SES. Support can verify the logs if the email does not arrive.
rejected: Just reset it. Enter your email and click the button. Check spam if it doesn't show.

prompt: Why is the Subscribe button greyed out on my profile?
chosen: The subscription button is temporarily disabled (disabled={true}) and shows '$7/month' because the self-service checkout portal is undergoing maintenance. Please contact support, and an administrator will manually upgrade your account role or quota in the database.
rejected: The portal is broken. We disabled the button. You can't upgrade right now.

prompt: What is the difference between the Free Plan and the Pro Plan?
chosen: The Free Plan is a default tier with a lifetime limit of 5 speech evaluations. The Pro Plan ($15/month) grants 25 evaluations per month and unlocks advanced Bedrock evaluations, sentence complexity analysis, rhetorical styling feedback, and unlimited classrooms.
rejected: Free gets you 5 total speeches. Pro gets you 25 a month. Pro is $15/month.

prompt: My Stripe payment succeeded, but my profile still shows I am on the Free plan. Why?
chosen: This is caused by a serialization error in our backend `/verify-payment` handler, which crashes when Stripe floats are written to DynamoDB without Decimal wrapping. Please contact support with your invoice reference, and an administrator will manually update your plan.
rejected: This is a backend database error. You'll need to wait for our engineers to fix the float serialization bug or try paying again later.

prompt: What happens to my old evaluations if I cancel my Pro subscription?
chosen: All your historical reports and speech files are fully preserved and remain accessible. However, you will be downgraded to the Free plan and blocked from uploading new videos if your total speeches exceed the Free plan limit.
rejected: If you cancel, you downgrade to free. We don't delete your old stuff, but you can't upload anything new.

prompt: Can I reactivate a canceled subscription?
chosen: Yes, if the current billing period has not expired, you can reactivate auto-renewal directly from your Profile tab by clicking the 'Renew Subscription' button.
rejected: Just click renew subscription if it's still active. Otherwise, you have to subscribe again.

prompt: Does my monthly quota rollover to the next month?
chosen: No. The monthly quota of 25 evaluations for the Pro plan resets to 0 upon renewal (triggered by Stripe's invoice.payment_succeeded webhook event) and does not roll over unused credits.
rejected: No, it resets to 0. Unused credits are lost.

prompt: Can I upgrade my account through the dashboard?
chosen: Self-service dashboard upgrades are currently disabled due to system maintenance on the checkout form. If you need Pro access, contact support so an admin can manually update your subscription status.
rejected: No, the upgrade button is disabled. You cannot upgrade right now.

prompt: How does the platform analyze my speech videos?
chosen: The backend runs AWS Transcribe to convert audio to text with timestamps and AWS Rekognition to track facial expressions frame-by-frame. These are evaluated by Amazon Bedrock (Nova Lite) to generate a structured Toastmaster feedback report.
rejected: We send your video to AWS to transcribe the audio and detect your facial emotions, and then use Bedrock to create a report.

instruction: What pacing target should I aim for in my speech?
chosen: You should aim for a conversational speaking rate of 130 to 150 Words Per Minute (WPM) to ensure the audience can follow and digest your content.
rejected: Aim for a speed of 130-150. Speeding up is bad, but going slow is boring.

prompt: How does the system measure silent pauses?
chosen: The engine scans the word timestamps. A pause is flagged if the gap between consecutive words is greater than 0.5 seconds. The system separates rhetorical pauses from hesitation silences based on length.
rejected: A pause is any gap over half a second. Some are good, some are bad.

prompt: What is the Pronunciation Clarity score?
chosen: It is the percentage of total words that exceed AWS Transcribe's confidence score threshold of 0.85. Words below this threshold are flagged as low-confidence words.
rejected: It's the percent of your words that the AI is confident about. The threshold is 0.85.

prompt: Which filler words are flagged by the application?
chosen: The regex compiler checks for: 'ah', 'uh', 'um', 'like', 'so', 'you know', 'actually', and 'basically'. It details counts and percentages of these verbal crutches.
rejected: Common fillers like um, ah, like, and actually.

prompt: How is visual sentiment analyzed?
chosen: AWS Rekognition processes video frames to monitor expressions: HAPPY, CALM, ANGRY, SAD, FEAR, SURPRISE, CONFUSED, and DISGUSTED. The system compiles the emotion distribution and dominant primaryEmotion.
rejected: Rekognition looks at your face and gets your emotions. It ranks them to find the primary one.

prompt: What template format does Amazon Bedrock use for evaluations?
chosen: The model is forced to output a structured JSON evaluation report matching the template in the master_evaluation table, including glows, grows, chronological reviews, and grammar checks.
rejected: Bedrock outputs a JSON template of Toastmaster feedback with glows, grows, and sections.

prompt: Why is my pronunciation clarity score so low?
chosen: This is often caused by speaking too fast, slurring, or background noise. We recommend rehearsing in a quiet room, speaking at a moderate pace, and using an external microphone.
rejected: Your pronunciation is unclear. Speak slower or use a better mic in a quiet room.

prompt: My video has been stuck in 'IN_PROGRESS' for over an hour. How do I fix it?
chosen: Analysis usually takes 1-3 minutes. If it is stuck, an AWS job or Bedrock call may have failed. A support agent can run `python reprocess_stuck_video.py <userId> <videoKey>` to check job status and reset the database status, or use `--force-restart` to restart the jobs.
rejected: Our servers are busy or the video failed. Contact support to run the backend reset script.

prompt: What causes the Bedrock 'Model use case details have not been submitted' error?
chosen: This error occurs because the AWS account holder has not submitted the Anthropic use case details form in the Bedrock console. The administrator must log into the AWS Console and complete this form to unlock access.
rejected: AWS is blocking our access because of a missing Anthropic use case details form. Tell your admin to fix it in the Bedrock console.

prompt: I see a float serialization error in logs. How do I bypass it?
chosen: This occurs because DynamoDB does not support native float types. In the backend handler, use python Decimal wrappers to format all float variables (such as subscription price or timestamps) before writing items to the database.
rejected: That's a database bug. DynamoDB hates floats. The developers need to change floats to Decimals in the backend lambda.

prompt: Why does the client get a CORS error when trying to fetch upload URLs locally?
chosen: CORS errors occur if the origin header of the local React app (like http://localhost:5173) does not match the allowed origins list defined in the backend configuration or CORS middleware headers.
rejected: CORS errors mean the backend configuration is blocking your local browser origin. Check your config.js or API settings.

prompt: What does the --force-restart flag do in the stuck video reprocess script?
chosen: The `--force-restart` flag tells the backend helper script to ignore previous AWS job statuses and trigger a fresh AWS Transcribe and Rekognition analysis pipeline from scratch.
rejected: It restarts the whole analysis pipeline from scratch if the AWS jobs failed.

prompt: How do students join an instructor's classroom?
chosen: Students join a classroom by copying the Class ID code provided by their instructor and pasting it into the enrollment field under the Profile tab, which links their account to the classroom dashboard.
rejected: Get the class ID from your teacher, go to Profile, paste it, and join.

prompt: How do custom evaluation rubrics work in classrooms?
chosen: Instructors can define custom evaluation criteria in the classroom settings. When a student in that class uploads a speech, the backend automatically overrides the default Toastmaster template with the custom rubric.
rejected: The teacher can override the standard Bedrock prompts with their own rubrics in class settings.

prompt: I sent coaching feedback to a student, but they didn't receive the email. Why?
chosen: Coaching feedback emails are sent via AWS SES. Verify that the student's email is correct in the dashboard, tell them to check spam, and ensure your custom coach email features are utilizing a verified SES sending domain.
rejected: SES failed or the email is wrong. Check the student's spam folder or database record.

prompt: How does the competition leaderboard rank participants?
chosen: The leaderboard ranks contestants using a composite score calculated from pronunciation clarity, pace alignment (closeness to 130-150 WPM), and filler word counts.
rejected: The leaderboard ranks users automatically based on their scores.

prompt: Why can't I see subscription pricing when enrolled in a class?
chosen: If you are a student active in a classroom, the frontend automatically hides subscription pricing options on your Profile page as your usage is governed under your class portal limits.
rejected: Because students in a class don't pay. The teacher's class subscription covers it.

prompt: How many times should I practice my presentation out loud?
chosen: For high-stakes presentations, experts recommend practicing out loud at least 10 times. The first few rounds help you internalize the content, while the remaining rounds let you refine delivery dynamics.
rejected: Rehearse it 10 times or as much as you can. It helps you memorize it.

prompt: How do I stop using fillers like 'um' and 'ah'?
chosen: Build real-time awareness by reviewing your speech reports. Practice replacing the filler word with a deliberate pause. Silence sounds thoughtful, whereas fillers can reduce your authority.
rejected: Just stop saying them. Use a pause instead when you think of what to say next.

prompt: Is it better to practice in front of a mirror or record a video?
chosen: Video recording is superior. Mirror practice is distracting because you self-correct in the moment, whereas video lets you watch your performance objectively as an audience member.
rejected: Use video. Mirrors are distracting and don't help you evaluate your presentation objectively.

prompt: Should I memorize my speech word-for-word?
chosen: No. Memorizing word-for-word often leads to a robotic delivery and increases panic if you forget a line. Memorize your Opening, Closing, and Transitions, and outline the middle sections.
rejected: No, you will forget it. Memorize only the intro and outro and wing the rest.

prompt: What is the 10-20-30 PowerPoint Rule?
chosen: It is a presentation guideline: limit your PowerPoint to no more than 10 slides, last no more than 20 minutes, and use a font size no smaller than 30 points to ensure clarity.
rejected: It means 10 slides, 20 minutes, and 30-point font. It keeps your slides clean.

prompt: Why is pacing important in public speaking?
chosen: Pacing controls how easily the audience digests information. The optimal rate is 130 to 150 WPM. Speaking too fast reduces comprehension, while speaking too slowly causes disengagement.
rejected: Pacing keeps the audience interested. Aim for 130-150 words per minute.

prompt: Is my rehearsal data private on this site?
chosen: Yes, all audio and video uploads are encrypted, stored securely in an Amazon S3 bucket, and are only accessible by you unless you choose to submit them to a class or competition.
rejected: Yes, we prioritize your privacy. Your videos are secure and only visible to you unless shared.

prompt: Do I need special equipment to use practiceyourspeech.com?
chosen: No special equipment is required. You only need a laptop or smartphone with a working camera and microphone. Rehearsing in a quiet, well-lit room will ensure the highest AI accuracy.
rejected: Just a phone or computer with a camera and microphone. Use a quiet room for better scores.

prompt: How do I make my technical presentations more engaging?
chosen: Focus on the story behind the data rather than just listing raw statistics. Utilize the 10-20-30 rule for slides and focus on how the findings impact the audience.
rejected: Don't just read data. Tell a story and keep slides short with big text.

prompt: What are the common filler words tracked by the system?
chosen: The platform tracks common verbal fillers including: 'ah', 'uh', 'um', 'like', 'so', 'you know', 'actually', and 'basically'. Reviewing these help identify repetitive speech habits.
rejected: The system flags filler words like um, ah, like, and actually so you can remove them.

prompt: What should I do if my audio quality is low in the analysis?
chosen: Ensure you are practicing in a quiet room with minimal background noise. Consider using an external USB microphone or headset to prevent echo and improve AWS Transcribe's accuracy.
rejected: Use a better microphone and find a quiet room. Noise makes the transcription bad.

prompt: How is WPM calculated on the backend?
chosen: WPM is calculated by taking the total word count from the transcription output and dividing by the speaking duration, measured as the difference between the end of the last word and the start of the first.
rejected: It takes the total count of words and divides by the speech duration.

prompt: Can a student leave a classroom after joining?
chosen: A student cannot self-remove from a classroom through the current frontend UI. The student must contact their instructor, who can remove them using the /remove-student-from-class endpoint.
rejected: No, only the instructor can remove you from the student list in the classroom settings.

prompt: What endpoint retrieves active speech competitions?
chosen: The /list-competitions GET/POST API endpoint retrieves a list of active, upcoming, and past speech contests from the SpeechCompetitions table in DynamoDB.
rejected: Use /list-competitions to get a list of speech contests.

prompt: What is the CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD for pronunciation clarity?
chosen: The system checks if the confidence score of each word is above a CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD of 0.85. Words below this threshold are categorized as low-confidence.
rejected: The threshold is 0.85 confidence score for AWS Transcribe words.

prompt: How does the instructor send custom grading rubrics to Bedrock?
chosen: The instructor sets rubrics in the classroom criteria. The backend retrieves this criteria override and injects it directly into the Amazon Bedrock LLM prompt template during speech evaluation.
rejected: The custom rubrics are saved in database and appended to the Bedrock prompt.

prompt: Where can organizers see participant results for a competition?
chosen: Organizers can access participant metrics and reports via the /get-competition-evaluations endpoint, which lists evaluated submissions and builds the leaderboard.
rejected: Go to the competition dashboard to see the evaluations and leaderboard.

prompt: Why does a video's status change to FAILED during analysis?
chosen: A status of FAILED occurs if the AWS Transcribe or Rekognition jobs throw errors, or if the Lambda Powertools logger records an unhandled execution timeout.
rejected: It means the processing jobs failed in the backend cloud services.

prompt: How do I check the number of evaluations I have left this month?
chosen: You can check your remaining speech quota in the Profile tab. The quota displays your active monthly count against the Pro Plan limit of 25 evaluations.
rejected: Look at the subscription details on your profile page to see your speech count.

prompt: What is the primaryEmotion attribute in the speech report?
chosen: The primaryEmotion attribute is the dominant facial expression identified by AWS Rekognition by aggregating expression counts throughout the video duration.
rejected: It is the face emotion that appeared the most in your video frames.

prompt: What email provider does the backend use to send welcome emails?
chosen: The backend utilizes Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) to send welcome emails, password reset links, and instructor coaching feedback notifications.
rejected: We use Amazon SES to send emails to our users.

prompt: What is the duration limit of a speech video in the free plan?
chosen: The Free plan does not impose direct duration limits, but speeches are limited by AWS Lambda execution timeouts. We recommend videos under 5 minutes.
rejected: We recommend videos under 5 minutes to avoid timeouts.

prompt: How can I check if my webcam is working for emotion tracking?
chosen: The frontend CameraView component shows a live preview. Ensure browser camera permissions are granted and you are centered in the frame.
rejected: Make sure your browser has permission and check the camera preview on the page.

prompt: How is a student's profile updated in the database when they join a class?
chosen: The /join-class endpoint updates the student's record in the SpeechUsers table by setting their classId attribute to the Class ID code.
rejected: The endpoint adds the Class ID to the student's user profile in DynamoDB.

prompt: What framework handles backend structured logging?
chosen: The python backend utilizes the AWS Lambda Powertools Logger and Tracer classes to inject structured logs and trace requests through AWS X-Ray.
rejected: We use AWS Lambda Powertools for logging and tracing in our python code.
